claims.text: The baseline alloy is an Al-free, equimolar Ti–V–Cr–Mn–Co high-entropy alloy.
The intervention adds 7 at.% Al while reducing Ti, V, Cr, Mn, and Co by equal atomic fractions.
Adding approximately 7 at.% Al induces nanoscale L12-ordered Al-rich precipitates.
The L12 precipitates obstruct dislocation glide.
Obstruction of dislocation glide by the L12 precipitates increases room-temperature yield strength.
The Al-rich precipitates act as a concentrated Al reservoir at the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
The proposed Al reservoir promotes rapid formation of a continuous protective Al2O3 scale.
The Al-modified alloy can simultaneously retain low density and achieve high mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The 7 at.% Al alloy will have at least 20% higher room-temperature yield strength than the Al-free baseline.
The 7 at.% Al alloy will have at least 50% lower oxidation mass gain than the baseline after 100 h in air at 800 °C.
The 7 at.% Al alloy will have a pitting potential equal to or higher than that of the baseline in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at room temperature.
The Al-free TiVCrMnCo baseline has a yield strength of approximately 750 MPa.
The Al-free baseline has an oxidation mass gain of approximately 2 mg/cm2 after 100 h at 800 °C.
The Al-free baseline has a pitting potential of approximately −0.2 V versus SCE in NaCl.
At temperatures of at least 900 °C, the L12 precipitates coarsen or transform.
At Al contents above 10 at.%, the L12 precipitates coarsen or transform.
Precipitate coarsening or transformation diminishes the combined strength and oxidation-resistance benefit.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least 20% higher yield strength and at least 50% lower oxidation mass gain, but the falsification rule uses 10% thresholds and only falsifies when neither performance metric improves by 10%. Thus, an alloy that misses both stated prediction thresholds—or improves only one property—may still evade falsification despite failing the proposed simultaneous-benefit outcome.
